evidence: src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: reserve() checks product.canReserve(quantity) for every line before calling product.reserve(quantity), so a reservation succeeds for all lines or none (a business rule).
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: totalByProduct() adds up order-line quantities per product (pure domain calculation).

src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: storage access goes only through the injected ProductRepository interface (findById/save), and the graph shows that interface is declared in src/domain/product-repository.ts.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: StockReservationService is a domain service. It holds business rules: it adds up quantities per product, checks stock with Product.canReserve before changing anything ("reserves every line or none"), and passes reserve/release to the Product aggregate. It throws domain errors (NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError). It reaches storage only through the ProductRepository interface, which is declared in the domain layer. That is the usual DDD port pattern, not a persistence detail. The file has no SQL, ORM, HTTP, framework or transport code, and no presentation concerns. Calling findById/save on a domain-owned repository abstraction from a domain service is a normal domain-layer job. One could argue that loading and saving belong in the application layer, but this coordination exists to enforce the all-or-nothing reservation rule, so it stays within the domain role. No ADR text was provided that says otherwise.
